props.name: CHE free-energy pathway of CO2RR to CH4 on both catalysts

evidence.quote: we further calculated the reaction pathway of the CO2RR to CH4 on CPF-Cu/CuNCs and raw CPF-Cu combined with the computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) model.

CO2 molecules were first transformed to the *COOH intermediate, and subsequently, *CO was generated from the *COOH intermediate through a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process. Then, *CHO, *CH2O, and *OCH3 intermediates were generated in turn by the reduction of *CO and further reduced to CH4.

On CPF-Cu/CuNCs, the hydrogenation of *CO to *CHO, which was considered the rate-limiting step for producing CH4 in the C1 hydrocarbon pathway, exhibited a smaller free energy change than that on CPF-Cu.
the free energy curve of the CO2RR for CPF-Cu/CuNCs was below that of CPF-Cu, suggesting that CPF-Cu/CuNCs was more favourable for the reaction.

The Cu NCs in CPF-Cu demonstrated stronger adsorption of intermediates and effectively lowered the energy levels, which could be clearly reflected by the smaller uphill climb in the free energy change of CO2 → *COOH, *CO → *CHO, and *CH2O →*CH3O. This result could be attributed to the stronger adsorption energy of the C1 intermediate at the dual active Cu-N4 + Cu NCs sites than at the individual Cu-N4 sites.

evidence.quote: CPF-Cu was prepared via solvothermal methods with 1,2,4,5-tetracyanobenzene (TCNB) as the conjugated ligand and copper chloride (CuCl2) as the central atom in the solvent of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF).
Based on the above results, dual active-site CPF-Cu/CuNCs catalysts containing uniformly dispersed Cu NCs and atomically dispersed Cu sites were successfully prepared.

evidence.quote: The electrochemical measurements were accomplished in a flow cell configuration at CHI 760E electrochemical workstation (Shanghai Chenhua, China). Platinum tablets and Hg/HgO electrodes were used as the counter and reference electrodes. An anion exchange membrane was used to separate the cathode compartment and anode compartment. And the aqueous KOH solution (1 M) was used as the electrolyte solution.

The catholyte solution and anolyte solution were separated at 40 mL·min−1 with a peristaltic pump, while CO2 gas was flowed to the gas chamber with a flow rate of 20 mL·min−1 by using a mass flow controller.

the tandem active centers realized the stepwise electrocatalytic reduction, during which the atomic Cu increased the dissociation of H2O while the Cu nanoclusters with a high electron density promoted the activation of CO2
In addition, CPF-Cu + Cu NCs presented a similar CH4 Faraday curve to that of CPF-Cu, which suggested that the lack of interactions between physically mixed CPF-Cu and Cu NCs limited CH4 production.
